title: Normalized right mates commute with a scalar square and counit-preserving equivalences
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_i,\mathcal D_i$ for $i=A,B$ be categories [def-nagata-category], with functors $F_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$, $G_i,H_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal C_i$, specified adjunctions $F_i\dashv G_i$ with counits $\epsilon_i$, and natural isomorphisms $\gamma_i:H_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i$. Put $z_{i,K}=\epsilon_{i,K}\circ F_i(\gamma_{i,K})$. Let $S:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal C_B$ and $T:\mathcal D_A\to\mathcal D_B$ be functors with natural isomorphisms $q:TF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BS$ and $a:SH_A\xrightarrow{\sim}H_BT$. Assume, for every $K\in\mathcal D_A$,
$$z_{B,TK}\circ F_B(a_K)\circ q_{H_AK}=T(z_{A,K}).$$
Let $b_K:SG_AK\to G_BTK$ be the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $T(\epsilon_{A,K})\circ q_{G_AK}^{-1}$. Then
$$b_K=\gamma_{B,TK}\circ a_K\circ S(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1}),$$
so $b$ is a natural isomorphism.

In addition, let $\mathcal C'_i,\mathcal D'_i$ be categories, $F'_i:\mathcal C'_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal D'_i:G'_i$ specified adjunctions with counits $\epsilon'_i$, and $U_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C'_i$, $V_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal D'_i$ equivalences (functors with quasi-inverses and natural isomorphisms from their two composites to the identity). Suppose given natural isomorphisms $c_i:V_iF_i\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_iU_i$ and $\rho_i:U_iG_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G'_iV_i$ satisfying the actual counit equation
$$\epsilon'_{i,V_iK}\circ F'_i(\rho_{i,K})\circ c_{i,G_iK}=V_i(\epsilon_{i,K}).$$
Let $S':\mathcal C'_A\to\mathcal C'_B$, $T':\mathcal D'_A\to\mathcal D'_B$ be functors and let $\delta_X:S'U_A\xrightarrow{\sim}U_BS$, $\delta_Y:T'V_A\xrightarrow{\sim}V_BT$, $q':T'F'_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_BS'$ be specified natural isomorphisms. Assume for every $M\in\mathcal C_A$ the specified square commutes:
$$F'_B(\delta_{X,M})\circ q'_{U_AM}\circ T'(c_{A,M})
=c_{B,SM}\circ V_B(q_M)\circ\delta_{Y,F_AM}.$$
Define the transported arrow with its endpoints explicitly by
$$\bar b_K=G'_B(\delta_{Y,K}^{-1})\circ\rho_{B,TK}\circ U_B(b_K)\circ\delta_{X,G_AK}\circ S'(\rho_{A,K}^{-1}).$$
Then the transported arrow is the specified right mate for $q'$:
$$\epsilon'_{B,T'V_AK}\circ F'_B(\bar b_K)
=T'(\epsilon'_{A,V_AK})\circ(q'_{G'_AV_AK})^{-1}.$$
All these equalities are natural in $K$ and $\bar b_K$ is invertible. They remain valid after replacing $V_AK$ by an isomorphic object, and hence identify the right mate on all of $\mathcal D'_A$. There is no additivity, tensor, sheaf, geometric or coefficient-ring hypothesis on this lemma beyond the explicitly stated functors and equations.

proof.text:
Put $u_K=\gamma_{B,TK}\circ a_K\circ S(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})$. The inverse Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] sends $v$ to $\epsilon_{B,TK}\circ F_B(v)$, and is injective. Compute
$$\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_{B,TK}F_B(u_K)
&=z_{B,TK}F_B(a_K)F_BS(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})\\
&=T(z_{A,K})q_{H_AK}^{-1}F_BS(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})\\
&=T(z_{A,K})TF_A(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})q_{G_AK}^{-1}
=T(\epsilon_{A,K})q_{G_AK}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality expands $z_B$, the second is the assumed normalization, the third is naturality of $q$ on $\gamma_{A,K}^{-1}$, and the last cancels $\gamma_A$ with its inverse. This is precisely the inverse transpose of $b_K$ by its definition, so injectivity gives $b_K=u_K$. Juxtaposition in all calculations means functional composition, rightmost map first.

proof.text: The expression $u=\gamma_B T\circ a\circ S\gamma_A^{-1}$ is a composite of whiskered natural isomorphisms. Its inverse has components $S(\gamma_{A,K})\circ a_K^{-1}\circ\gamma_{B,TK}^{-1}$: composing in either order cancels three adjacent inverse pairs. Naturality follows by applying the given naturality equations to these composites (inverse naturality follows by multiplying the original equation by the inverses). Thus $b$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of transposes: conjugate the normalized right-adjoint model, then substitute the site counit and the site/coefficient square; returned parent proof Steps 4–5, isolated as an abstract lemma.

proof.text:
For the second assertion fix $K$ and abbreviate $M=G_AK$, $r=\rho_{A,K}$, $d=\delta_{Y,K}$, $e=\epsilon_{A,K}$, $C=c_{A,M}$, $p=q'_{U_AM}$, and $E=\epsilon'_{B,T'V_AK}\circ F'_B(\bar b_K)$. Expanding $\bar b$ and cancelling $S'(r^{-1})S'(r)$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
E F'_BS'(r)
&=d^{-1}\epsilon'_{B,V_BTK}F'_B(\rho_{B,TK})F'_BU_B(b_K)F'_B(\delta_{X,M})\\
&=d^{-1}V_B(\epsilon_{B,TK})c_{B,G_BTK}^{-1}F'_BU_B(b_K)F'_B(\delta_{X,M})\\
&=d^{-1}V_B(\epsilon_{B,TK}F_B(b_K))c_{B,SM}^{-1}F'_B(\delta_{X,M})\\
&=d^{-1}V_BT(e)V_B(q_M^{-1})c_{B,SM}^{-1}F'_B(\delta_{X,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
These four equalities use, respectively, naturality of $\epsilon'_B$ on $d^{-1}$, the assumed $B$ counit equation, naturality of $c_B$ on the actual arrow $b_K:SM\to G_BTK$, and the defining transpose identity proved in Step 1. Every term has source $F'_BS'U_AM$ and target $T'V_AK$.

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of transposes: conjugate the normalized right-adjoint model, then substitute the site counit and the site/coefficient square; returned parent proof Steps 4–5, isolated as an abstract lemma.

proof.text:
The assumed square at $M$, solved by multiplying by its specified inverses, reads
$$V_B(q_M^{-1})c_{B,SM}^{-1}F'_B(\delta_{X,M})=\delta_{Y,F_AM}\,T'(C^{-1})p^{-1}.$$
Substitute this in Step 3. Naturality of $\delta_Y:T'V_A\to V_BT$ on $e:F_AM\to K$ gives
$$d^{-1}V_BT(e)\delta_{Y,F_AM}=T'V_A(e).$$
Consequently
$$E F'_BS'(r)=T'(V_A(e)C^{-1})p^{-1}.$$
This uses only the displayed square and naturality, with no identification of a chosen comparison with an identity.

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of transposes: conjugate the normalized right-adjoint model, then substitute the site counit and the site/coefficient square; returned parent proof Steps 4–5, isolated as an abstract lemma.

proof.text:
The $A$ counit equation gives $V_A(e)C^{-1}=\epsilon'_{A,V_AK}F'_A(r)$. Naturality of $q'$ on $r:U_AM\to G'_AV_AK$ gives
$$T'F'_A(r)p^{-1}=(q'_{G'_AV_AK})^{-1}F'_BS'(r).$$
Thus
$$E F'_BS'(r)=T'(\epsilon'_{A,V_AK})(q'_{G'_AV_AK})^{-1}F'_BS'(r).$$
Since $r$ is an isomorphism, cancel the rightmost factor. This proves exactly the asserted counit identity for $\bar b_K$. The Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], with $F'_B\dashv G'_B$, makes that identity characterize the transpose uniquely; hence $\bar b_K$ is the specified right mate of $q'$, as defined in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of transposes: conjugate the normalized right-adjoint model, then substitute the site counit and the site/coefficient square; returned parent proof Steps 4–5, isolated as an abstract lemma.

proof.text:
All factors in the definition of $\bar b$ are whiskerings of natural isomorphisms, including $U_Bb$ by Step 2; therefore $\bar b$ is natural and invertible, its inverse being obtained by reversing the factors and inverting each. The mate of $(q')^{-1}$ is a natural transformation on all of $\mathcal D'_A$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and Step 5 identifies its restriction along $V_A$ with $\bar b$. For any isomorphism $j:V_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}K'$, its component at $K'$ is explicitly
$$G'_BT'(j)\circ\bar b_K\circ S'G'_A(j^{-1}),$$
by that naturality. This is invertible and independent of the presentation because it equals the already specified mate component. A quasi-inverse $W_A$ of $V_A$ supplies such a $j:V_AW_AK'\cong K'$ for every $K'$. This proves the final replacement and exhaustivity claims without any extra geometric or coefficient hypothesis.
